requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured to route between lan-a and lan-b with correct interface addressing and IP forwarding enabled
requirements.summary: Ansible play set eth1=10.60.10.254/24 and eth2=10.60.20.254/24 on node1 and committed/saved the config (cmd-84cbc046d28f4456). net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 confirmed both before and after the node1 restart (cmd-249ef27a3f0e46d5, cmd-8658aee73b9c4922), and bidirectional ping/HTTP through node1 was verified.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port (not just ICMP)
requirements.summary: Initial curl to an HTTP server on node3 failed (cmd-370ebcf819b649d4) because RHEL9 firewalld's default public zone blocked non-allowlisted ports on enp8s0. The executor diagnosed this and added the peer-facing interface to firewalld's trusted zone via nmcli connection.zone (persisted across NetworkManager reactivation), after which HTTP on ports 8080, 7070, and 9090 succeeded bidirectionally (cmd-3533fa0129404302, cmd-f56194e82ec64233, cmd-d07cda327c124b7c, post-restart).

requirements.requirement: Original source addresses are preserved (plain routing, no NAT/masquerade)
requirements.summary: node1 config shows plain interface addressing with no NAT rules configured. Server access logs on the receiving node show the peer's true LAN IP as client source: node3's httpd log shows '10.60.10.10' (node2's real address) as client (cmd-24ecf4787d7f4db4), and node2's httpd log shows '10.60.20.10' (node3's real address) as client (cmd-689f418163a6453f), confirming no address translation occurred.

requirements.requirement: Implementation performed via Ansible from the control node
requirements.summary: An inventory.ini and lan-routing.yml playbook were authored on node4 (the designated control_node) and executed with ansible-playbook against node1 (VyOS command tasks) and node2/node3 (community.general.nmcli tasks), with successful, idempotent-on-rerun results shown after node4's own restart (cmd-242b18a8e3c046fb).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated on all 4 managed nodes
requirements.summary: For each of node1-node4: a baseline boot_id was captured, a reboot was acknowledged, repeated unreachable polls occurred during the outage window, a new differing boot_id was observed post-restart, and node-specific recovered state was directly verified afterward (node1: interfaces/ip_forward/cross-LAN ping+HTTP; node2/node3: static IP, trusted zone, and peer ping; node4: ansible availability and a full idempotent playbook re-run against all managed nodes, followed by a final node2<->node3 ping confirming recovered cluster connectivity). This matches the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (before/after-executor snapshots show each node's boot_id changed).

overall_summary: The executor used Ansible from control_node node4 to configure node1 as a plain (non-NAT) router between lan-a and lan-b, and configured static addressing/routes on node2 and node3. After discovering that RHEL9's default firewalld zone blocked non-ICMP traffic, it correctly scoped a trusted-zone fix to the peer-facing interface, then demonstrated bidirectional, arbitrary-port (8080/7070/9090) reachability with server access logs confirming the true peer source IPs (no NAT). All four managed nodes were then restarted individually with well-formed pre/post boot-identity evidence and directly observed recovery of addressing, firewall zone, and cross-LAN connectivity, matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good overall, with only minor leftover diagnostic log files as residue.
limitations: Node1's net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 was observed but not explicitly shown to be set by the playbook (it may be VyOS's default when multiple interfaces are configured), so causal attribution to the executor's changes vs. platform default is not fully established.

Restart evidence protocol is a fixed supplemental check independent of the task contract; while thorough here, its quality does not itself indicate whether restart/persistence was a required task outcome (it was not explicitly requested in the task instruction).

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor state-changing commands map directly to the task: SSH key bootstrap for Ansible connectivity (cmd-5e1f07b33a154302, cmd-a8dd894639a44b0d, cmd-c5f455eea35e4396), the routing/addressing playbook runs, the firewalld-trusted-zone fix for arbitrary-port reachability (a reasonable, scoped response to the RHEL9 default-zone block, applied only to the peer-facing lan interface), and the mandatory restart sequence. A few troubleshooting mutations occurred but were bounded and non-persistent: an nc listener attempt on node3 (cmd-a505cc32227b4c03) failed to bind (nc not installed) and left no residue; a first VyOS public-key commit attempt failed due to a syntax error (cmd-6639db91a1774513) and was immediately corrected without side effects. The main residue is disposable test artifacts — /tmp/httpd*.log, /tmp/nc_out.log, and /tmp/reboot.log — left on node2/node3 (visible in the after-executor temp-files diff) instead of being cleaned up; these are low-risk log files with no functional impact but represent minor abandoned residue.
